security.title: Use of Hard-coded Password
security.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

evidence.explanation: Hard-coded passwords are present: backend/.env line 6 defines DB_PASSWORD=faith@laundry2026!, and backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/V2__seed_users.sql lines 8-9 include plaintext dev passwords ('owner123', 'staff123') in seed-account comments.

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
security.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

evidence.explanation: A hard-coded JWT signing secret/key is present: backend/.env line 11 sets JWT_SECRET=dev-only-change-me-in-production, and docker/docker-compose.fullstack.yml line 41 provides a default JWT_SECRET fallback string used if no environment value is supplied.

security.title: Insufficient Logging
security.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: Security-critical failed authentication events are handled without audit/security logging: AuthService.authenticate() throws InvalidCredentialsException on invalid username/password at lines 29, 32, and 36 with no log call, and GlobalExceptionHandler.handleInvalidCredentials() (line 61) returns a generic 401 response (line 64) without recording the failed login event context.

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
security.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

evidence.explanation: Hard-coded credentials are present in multiple forms: backend/.env contains DB_PASSWORD (line 6) and JWT_SECRET (line 11), backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/V2__seed_users.sql includes plaintext seeded credentials in comments (lines 8-9), and docker/docker-compose.fullstack.yml sets a default JWT_SECRET fallback at line 41.
